Also count listening with the screen off?

Music, podcasts and audiobooks that play while the screen is off are not screen time, so they are not counted today. To count them, Schirmziit needs notification access — that is the only way Android lets an app see which app is playing. Schirmziit never reads your notifications and never what is playing, only that something is.
This phone stops sending screen time. Nothing already sent is deleted, and your parents keep seeing the days up to now. A parent has to sign in for this, so nobody can switch it off on their own.

Schirmziit shows how long and when your child\'s phone is used. None of it is secret: the child sees the same numbers on their own phone.
On your family\'s own server, in your own database. No company in between and nothing passed to third parties.
Hourly figures stay 13 months, then only daily totals. You can delete a child\'s data at any time.
Schirmziit blocks nothing and filters nothing. It is a basis for a conversation, not a remote control.
Schirmziit shows numbers, not advice. How much screen time makes sense, and what helps when it turns into an argument, is better explained by these Swiss organisations:
The federal platform: age guidance, rules, leaflets for parents.
Concrete guide values per age and tips for family agreements.
Free counselling for children and teenagers, around the clock — phone, chat or SMS.
Swiss centre for media literacy: parent evenings, courses, counselling.
Made in Switzerland. Free and open source.
